articleHeadline: Typhoid control needs more vaccine, less antibiotic
articleSummary: Typhoid cases are rising in India, but control relies on vaccination and diagnostics rather than antibiotics alone. Diagnosis is hindered by unreliable tests: Widal lacks specificity in endemic settings, and blood culture sensitivity is only ~55–60%, worsened by prior antibiotic exposure, fueling antimicrobial resistance and surveillance gaps. The WHO prioritizes typhoid-conjugate vaccines (TCV); India produced Typbar-TCV (WHO prequalified since 2017) and other Indian TCVs have prequalification, but vaccination scale remains inadequate within an integrated control strategy that also includes water, sanitation, and diagnostics. Key recommendations: strengthen surveillance with documentation of suspected and culture-confirmed cases and antimicrobial susceptibility; diagnostic stewardship—obtain blood cultures before antibiotics with adequate volume; invest in better rapid diagnostics; and revisit TCV’s role in public-health planning to achieve both vaccination and prevention.

articleSummary: New Delhi, India, during the monsoon, fever, body aches, headache and weakness can be caused by dengue, malaria or chikungunya, with early symptoms often overlapping and insufficient to distinguish among them. Dengue features sudden high fever, severe headache, retro-orbital pain, muscle and joint pain, nausea/vomiting and sometimes a rash; a critical phase can occur as fever subsides. Chikungunya is marked by severe joint pain and may include fever, muscle pain, rash and fatigue; joint pain can persist for weeks to months. Malaria presents with fever, headache and chills; the classic fever–chills–sweating cycle is not universal. Timing of tests matters: dengue NS1 and molecular tests useful early; antibody testing later. Chikungunya detectable by molecular tests in first week; malaria via microscopy or rapid diagnostic tests. Severe dengue signs during fever decline require urgent care. Avoid self-medication; antibiotics don’t treat dengue/chikungunya; malaria requires antimalarials; NSAIDs are avoided in dengue; paracetamol as advised.

articleSummary: Researchers at the University of São Paulo (USP), with FAPESP support, developed an electronic tongue that detects antibodies against avian influenza H5N1 within about six minutes. articleSummary: Dengue fever guidance in Vietnam emphasizes vigilant care during the first three days to prevent progression to severe disease. Dengue typically begins with sudden high fever and symptoms such as headache, muscle/joint pain, retro-orbital ache, nausea, and poor appetite; the dangerous phase often emerges as fever subsides, around days 3–7. Five actions are advised in the initial three days: (1) seek medical evaluation to confirm dengue and tailor treatment, especially for those with chronic illnesses or other risk factors; (2) maintain adequate hydration with oral fluids; avoid at-home IV therapy unless prescribed; (3) manage fever with paracetamol per medical guidance; avoid aspirin or ibuprofen; (4) monitor beyond temperature—track fluids in/out, urine volume, abdominal pain, vomiting, bleeding, mental status, and breathing; (5) seek urgent care if warning signs develop (severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, mucosal bleeding, dark stools, rapid breathing, lethargy). Fever alone does not mean recovery; close monitoring is essential to prevent plasma leakage and organ injury.

articleSummary: Mpox (Monkeypox) transmission modeled in Indonesia by Hasanuddin University researchers to explore multi-measure outbreak control. WHO warns the outbreak remains uncontrolled and could become among the worst. The Bundibugyo variant lacks an approved vaccine or treatment; vaccination of frontline workers is underway with Ervebo (Zaire variant), and trials for a Bundibugyo-specific vaccine are in progress. Cross-border risk to Uganda persists after Uganda ended its own outbreak last month.

articleHeadline: Her Back Pain Was Treated as Tuberculosis for a Year Before Sequencing Found a Parasite in Her Spine
articleSummary: Chengdu, a 28-year-old woman presented with seven months of back pain from T12-L2, with abscess. She was treated as spinal tuberculosis for 12 months after exposure and prior TB treatment, including surgery to remove a lesion. Pathology showed granulomatous inflammation with caseous necrosis, but acid-fast stain was negative. Despite standard anti-TB therapy, imaging worsened and a new abscess appeared. On a second operation, pus was sent for metagenomic sequencing, identifying Echinococcus multilocularis, cause of alveolar echinococcosis. Anti-TB drugs were stopped; albendazole at 20 mg/kg/day (max 1 g/day) in 30-day courses with 14-day breaks. Three months after discharge, imaging improved; at six months, back pain and numbness largely resolved. The report notes anchoring bias and missed serology, and states alveolar echinococcosis can spread to spine and lungs, with higher incidence in Central Asia and western China, transmitted by canids via eggs in feces. Eight years separated liver surgery from spinal symptoms.

articleSummary: Meningococcal meningitis remains a serious, evolving threat in Brazil, with mortality estimated at 20–30%, especially in children under five and older adults. Neisseria meningitidis causes this meningitis, with six serogroups (A,B,C,W,Y); vaccines cover A,C,W,Y, while serogroup B vaccine is available only in the private sector. Brazil’s National Immunization Program provides meningococcal C vaccine at 3 and 5 months, and ACWY boosters at 12 months and 11–14 years. Since C vaccination began publicly in 2010, invasive meningococcal disease cases fell by over 80% from about 3,000 annually. Yet serogroup B now predominates, responsible for 69% of notifications in babies under 1 year in 2025. Disease can progress within 24 hours: initial symptoms (fever, headache, irritability, sore throat, runny nose, nausea, vomiting, drowsiness) in the first 8 hours; neck stiffness, photophobia, rash, cold extremities by 9–15 hours; seizures or altered consciousness by 16–24 hours. Vaccination against B and ACWY at recommended ages is advised; seek care promptly.

articleHeadline: El brote de ébola sigue fuera de control: Congo suma 6.000 casos y 3.000 muertos
articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo remains out of control. As of August 29, 2026, the Ministry of Communication and Media reports 6,041 confirmed infections and 2,911 deaths, a case-fatality rate of 48.2%. The Congo outbreak has surpassed 6,000 cases and nearly 3,000 deaths. Conditions hindering containment include insecurity, displacement, a strike by health workers, and large-scale population movements. The World Health Organization warns the epidemic is spreading under extreme difficulty, and is on a trajectory to surpass Africa’s 2014–2016 Ebola outbreak—the deadliest on record, which killed more than 11,000, mainly in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone. The report highlights ongoing transmission and the significant challenges faced in the eastern Congo.
notes: 発生地域にLiberia, Guinea, Sierra Leoneが含まれるが、これらは2014-2016年の過去流行との比較として言及されているのみで、現在の発生国ではないため除外。対象国リストにも含まれていない。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Last week, Hanoi recorded 268 dengue fever cases.
articleHeadline: Tuần qua, Hà Nội ghi nhận 268 trường hợp mắc sốt xuất huyết
articleSummary: 268 dengue fever cases were recorded in Hanoi last week (Aug 21–28, 2026), across 74 wards/communes, down from 309 the week before. Cumulatively for 2026, Hanoi has 2,175 dengue cases in 117 wards/communes, below the 5‑year average (2,708) and well below 2023’s 6,897. Twelve new dengue outbreaks were identified this week; year‑to‑date there are 91 outbreaks with 30 currently active. Hand, foot, and mouth disease reached 115 cases in 58 wards/communes (down from 176); total 4,830 cases in 2026, with no deaths, across 126 wards. Measles: 4 cases in 3 wards; cumulative 392 in 110 wards. Pertussis: 2 cases in 4 wards; cumulative 103 in 56 wards. COVID-19: 53 cases in 35 wards; cumulative 1,577 in 121 wards. CDC Hanoi intensified surveillance, mapping with Google Maps, and 24/7 rapid response teams over the National Day holiday; emphasis on vaccination, water container hygiene, bed nets, and seeking care for fever.
notes: デング熱、手足口病、麻疹、百日咳、COVID-19いずれも例年平均以下または横ばいで推移する定例報告。死亡例も報告されておらず、ルーチンの公衆衛生モニタリング情報と判断。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Two youths from Congo who arrived in Agra tested positive for Ebola; the health department has put the entire family under home quarantine.
articleHeadline: कांगो से आगरा आए दो युवक निकले इबोला पॉजिटिव, स्वास्थ्य विभाग ने पूरे परिवार को किया होम क्वारंटाइन - agra youths from congo test ebola positive home isolated
articleSummary: Two youths returning from Congo tested positive for Ebola in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India. Health department teams visited their home after airport testing confirmed infection; both are under home isolation along with family, with medicines supplied and ongoing monitoring. The Congo Ebola outbreak prompted airport sampling for travelers arriving in India; the 32-year-old arrived August 28 in Mumbai with Ebola tests conducted at the airport before departure, while the other youth reached India via Delhi on August 28, with samples also collected at the Delhi airport. Lab results were forwarded to Agra’s health officials, who confirmed Ebola virus infection in both individuals. Both patients are not showing severe symptoms. Officials emphasized the cases are imported; the family is under home quarantine as authorities continue surveillance.
notes: 記事内容にはエボラ陽性者が自宅隔離とされている点で医学的整合性に疑義がある（通常エボラは専門医療機関での厳重隔離が必要）。誤報・誤診の可能性も含め続報の確認が必要。DRCは感染源国として言及されているが、実際の発症確認地はインドのため、verified_locationsにはIndiaのみを記載。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Coliform bacteria detected in dining bowls at restaurants across Guangdong exceed safety standards.
articleHeadline: 广东多地餐饮店餐碗被检出大肠菌群超标_YNET.com北青网
articleSummary: On 25 Aug, Guangdong Market Supervision Administration announced 17 of 613 sampled foods failed safety standards across six categories (drinks, tea products, aquatic products, pastries, egg products, catering foods). Microbial contamination led the noncompliance: self-disinfecting bowls in Guangzhou outlets tested with coliforms (one also with anionic detergents); a Guangzhou Meituan-delivered white-cut chicken batch exceeded total plate counts and Escherichia coli; bottled waters from Dongguan tested positive for Pseudomonas aeruginosa; a Zhanjiang dried mussel batch contained lead. Other issues included overuse of food coloring in tea products and a high peroxide value in a fried iron-spoon pastry. Nanhai District's Foshan eatery and other outlets were cited for additional bowl-related contamination. The regulator requires investigations, product removals/recalls, and public disclosure. The article notes hot-water rinsing may reduce but not eliminate bacteria, with effectiveness varying by temperature and duration.
notes: 市場監督管理局による通常の食品安全モニタリング（抜き取り検査）の結果報告であり、感染症アウトブレイクの兆候ではない。具体的な健康被害（発症・入院・死亡）の報告はない。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Girl develops over 20 "pearly papules" all over her body after swimming for more than 20 days; doctors warn: pools are high-risk transmission zones—don't squeeze, or it will spread.
articleHeadline: 女孩游泳20多天后全身竟冒出20多个"小珍珠"，医生提醒：泳池是传播高危区，不要挤，会传染
articleSummary: Henan Province, China reports a molluscum contagiosum case in a girl after more than 20 days of swimming in summer, who developed over 20 pearly, waxy, dome-shaped papules with a central tiny navellike indentation all over her body. Lesions are usually painless but can spread via scratching; squeezing can eject white curd-like material containing active virus, greatly increasing transmission. Transmission occurs through direct skin contact, contact with contaminated items (towels, swim gear), or autoinoculation to other body parts. Pools in summer are high-risk zones since the virus can survive in moist, warm environments and is hard to eliminate with standard chlorine. Prevention emphasizes skin-barrier protection and hygiene: moisturize before swimming, rinse and dry thoroughly afterward, avoid sharing items, choose well-maintained pools, and treat minor skin injuries promptly. Sources: Guangming Online, Urban Channel, Zhejiang University Children's Hospital Dermatology. 2026-09-01.
notes: 記事は河南省の一事例を扱う健康啓発記事であり、Bluedotが付与した浙江省・中国の地域タグは病院情報源(浙江大学児童病院)に由来する可能性が高く、実際の発生地は河南省。伝染性軟属腫は対象国での重大な公衆衛生イベントには該当しないためverified_locationsは空とした。

articleHeadlineTranslated: With the expected intensification of the Super El Niño, Hortolândia's population should step up precautions against Aedes aegypti - Portal Veloz.
articleHeadline: Com intensificação prevista do Super El Niño, população de Hortolândia deve redobrar cuidados contra Aedes aegypti - Portal Veloz
articleSummary: As the Super El Niño is expected to intensify in Brazil from September 2026, Hortolândia increases Aedes aegypti precautions. Meteorological forecasts warn of heat waves and storms, elevating dengue risk. The Unidade Vigilância de Zoonoses (UVZ) conducts house-to-house inspections in Parque Vasconcelos, Recanto do Sol and Vila Real, following high ADL (Análise de Densidade Larvária) in July. Agents remove breeding sites and educate residents, noting about 80% of mosquito larvae are inside homes; residents are asked to allow entry. UVZ contact: (19) 3897-3312 or (19) 3897-5974 for route updates. Dengue vaccination is available at seven UBS clinics, with extended hours: until 17:30 at Amanda II, Dom Bruno Gamberini, Rosolém, and Santa Clara; until 18:30 at Amanda I, Figueiras, and Parque do Horto, in addition to 7:30–15:30 vaccination hours.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in DR Congo: Cases exceed 6,000; death toll climbs to 3,000, WHO says it's out of control.
articleHeadline: ยอดป่วยอีโบลาดีอาร์คองโก "ทะลุ 6 พันราย" เซ่นพุ่ง 3 พันคน WHO เผยคุมไม่ได้
articleSummary: DR Congo Ebola outbreak surpasses 6,000 confirmed cases with at least 2,911 deaths and over 1,360 recoveries, as of Aug 29–Sept 1, 2026. The fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history has spread to 60 health zones in the eastern provinces of Ituri and North Kivu. WHO says the situation remains uncontrolled and could be more severe than the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic, which killed over 11,000 mainly in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone. On Aug 29, an armed youth attack targeted a funeral security convoy in Mambasa, Ituri, illustrating insecurity that hampers response and raises transmission risk at burial sites. Burials and corpse handling pose high infection risk. Ervebo vaccination has begun for healthcare workers and frontline responders; Ervebo targets Zaire ebolavirus, while Bundibugyo strain is in clinical trials. Ongoing challenges include displacement and health worker strikes.
notes: 記事はDRCのイツリ州・北キブ州でのエボラ流行を主題としている。2014-2016年西アフリカ流行（ギニア・リベリア・シエラレオネ）は歴史的比較対象として言及されているのみで、現在の発生地ではないため verified_locations から除外した。武装勢力による治安悪化・埋葬時の感染リスク・医療従事者ストライキなど対応を困難にする要因が複数存在し、WHOも制御不能と評価しており緊急性が高い。
